cards.text: God's servant John is being shown a vision (Revelation 1:1). He just watched the Lamb, Jesus (John 1:29), open the sixth seal, and people on earth were asking who is able to withstand it (Revelation 6:12-17). Now, after this, John sees four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, and every one of them is holding something back.

cards.question: The angels at the four corners of the earth are holding back its four ___.
With the four winds held back, the sea stays calm but the land still gets a breeze.

cards.text: Then John sees another angel coming up from the east, carrying the seal of the living God. And this one is NOT whispering when he calls out in a loud voice to the four angels.

cards.question: The angel with the seal calls out to the four angels at the corners of the earth. What had those four been given power to do?

answers.text: Harm the land and the sea
Open the seals on the scroll

cards.text: His message to them is basically: not yet. Friend, it's grabbing somebody's arm one second before they hit send on the group chat.

cards.question: The angel tells the four angels not to harm the land, the sea or the trees until something happens first. What is it?
The angel says the seal goes on the ___ of the servants of our God.

cards.text: Then John hears the number of those who were sealed. 144,000.

cards.question: Where do the 144,000 who were sealed come from?

cards.text: Then John hears it tribe by tribe, starting with Judah and ending with Benjamin: twelve tribes, 12,000 sealed from each one. Friend, I shared a drawer with a stack of receipts nobody would ever need, and NOT ONE of them was this organized.

After this, John looks and sees a multitude too large to count, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. Friend, I counted falling dust for FUN in that junk drawer, and even I would give up on this crowd.

cards.question: Where does this multitude too large to count come from?

answers.text: Every nation and tribe and tongue

cards.question: The multitude standing before the throne is dressed in sackcloth, like people in mourning.

cards.text: They're wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands. Then the whole multitude cries out in a loud voice.

cards.question: The multitude cries out: salvation to our ___, who sits on the throne, and to the ___!

cards.text: All the angels are standing around the throne, around the elders and the four living creatures who are around God's throne (Revelation 4:4, 6). Then the angels fall facedown before the throne and worship God.

Between an Amen at the start and an Amen at the end, they give God blessing, glory, wisdom, thanks, honor, power and strength. That's SEVEN in a row, friend, and I've only got six toppings and I STILL mix those up.

cards.question: The angels give God blessing, glory, honor and more, and they say it's His for a little while.

cards.text: Then one of the elders turns to John with a question about all these people in white robes.

cards.question: The elder asks John two things about the people in white robes. Which two?

answers.text: Who they are and where they came from
How many there are and when they came
What their names are and who sent them

cards.text: John calls the elder sir and tells him he's the one who knows. Friend, I'm STEALING that move for the next time somebody asks me something I can't answer.

cards.question: So the elder tells John who the people in white robes are. What have they come out of?
The elder says the people in white robes have washed their robes and made them white in the ___ of the Lamb.

cards.text: For this reason, they're before the throne of God, serving Him day and night in His temple. And the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.

cards.question: The elder says the people in white robes will still hunger and thirst, just less than before.

cards.text: Never again will they hunger or thirst, and no sun or scorching heat will beat down on them. Friend, I stand next to a hot oven ALL day, so that last part has Papa LISTENING.

cards.question: The elder tells John who will be the shepherd of the people in white robes. Who is it?

answers.text: The Lamb in the center of the throne
One of the elders by the throne
The angel who came from the east

cards.question: The Lamb will lead them to springs of living ___, and God will wipe away every ___ from their eyes.

cards.text: Hold that picture, friend. John's vision keeps going after this, and so do we.

findings.problem: The joke compares the angel's 'not yet' to grabbing someone's arm before they hit send on the group chat. That image is about stopping a rash message someone would regret. In Revelation 7:3 the harm isn't a mistake being stopped. It's held back until God's servants are sealed. So the comparison has a different action, and it hints that the coming harm is a regrettable outburst. Use an everyday image of holding something until a task is done first, like holding the doors until everyone is on board.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
